revision_reason: Revised to incorporate review feedback on fnmatch matching semantics (blocking #1) and missing Session model persistence test task (blocking #2). Verified architect's revision 2 addresses both blocking items. Added new risks R-10 (directory expansion scope explosion) and R-11 (warn counter increment timing). Upgraded risk granularity and added concrete disagreements.
title: Risk assessment: Enforce per-task file restrictions from planner in implement phase
risk_summary: The proposed implementation is well-designed and builds on proven infrastructure. The primary risks are operational (planner file lists too narrow, directory expansion more permissive than intuitive) rather than security (existing path normalization and traversal prevention cover the new code paths). Two new risks identified in this revision: (1) directory expansion can cause 'scope explosion' where a single root-level file grants access to an entire subtree, weakening containment for common layouts; (2) warn-then-block counter increments even on pushes that fail at later validation layers, causing premature blocking. Both are mitigatable with implementation-time fixes.

blocking_feedback_1_fnmatch_semantics.assessment: The architect chose option (b) from the reviewer's suggestion — explicitly acknowledge recursive matching and update all documentation/tests accordingly. This is the correct choice: changing to segment-aware matching (PurePosixPath.match) would be a breaking change affecting all existing phase restriction patterns (e.g., `.egg-state/contracts/*` currently matches nested files and production relies on this). DD-2 is updated, edge cases are corrected, test task-9 now requires explicit recursive behavior verification including boundary cases, and the plan template task-7 documents the semantics. The key remaining risk is that recursive matching provides coarser containment than the feature name ('per-task file restrictions') implies — see R-10 below.
blocking_feedback_1_fnmatch_semantics.verification: Independently confirmed via Python 3: fnmatch.fnmatch('dir/sub/deep/file.py', 'dir/*') returns True. PurePosixPath('dir/sub/deep/file.py').match('dir/*') returns False. The existing _matches_pattern() at phase_filter.py:243 uses fnmatch for all '*'-containing patterns, confirming this is existing production behavior.

blocking_feedback_2_session_persistence_.assessment: The architect added task-8 (Session model persistence tests) in Phase 5, covering: (a) allowed_files round-trip serialization, (b) backward compatibility for sessions without allowed_files, (c) _warned_files initialization and non-persistence. Tasks were correctly renumbered. The test file (gateway/tests/test_session_manager.py) is added to files_affected. Acceptance criteria are specific and testable.

risks.title: fnmatch recursive matching is coarser containment than feature name implies
risks.description: Python's fnmatch.fnmatch() treats `*` as matching `/`, so the directory expansion pattern `dir/*` grants recursive access to the entire `dir/` subtree, not just immediate children. This means per-task file restrictions operate at directory-subtree granularity, not individual file granularity. Users and planners may expect finer control than the system actually provides. For example, listing `src/auth/login.py` grants access to `src/auth/utils/deep/helper.py`.
risks.mitigation: Architect's revision 2 correctly acknowledges this and documents it throughout (DD-2, edge cases, tests, plan template). The 'guide, don't cage' philosophy accepts this tradeoff. Tests explicitly verify the recursive behavior. No code change needed — documentation is the mitigation.
risks.previous: Flagged as HIGH severity in revision 1 when the plan incorrectly claimed shallow matching

risks.title: Warn counter increments on pushes that fail at later validation layers
risks.description: The per-task validation layer runs BEFORE phase restrictions (Layer 3 before Layer 4 per DD-10). If a push contains a file that triggers a per-task warning (counter incremented) but the push is then BLOCKED by phase restrictions, the push fails but the warn counter was already incremented. On the next attempt (after fixing the phase issue), the same file would be BLOCKED by per-task restrictions because the counter shows a prior 'warning' that never actually resulted in a successful push. The agent never benefited from the warning but lost its free pass.
risks.mitigation: Implementation should only increment _warned_files counters AFTER all validation layers pass (i.e., at the end of the push handler, before forwarding to git). Alternatively, the per-task layer can return a 'pending warning' that the push handler commits to _warned_files only on overall success. This is a ~5 line change: collect pending warnings, apply them after all checks pass.
risks.recommendation: MUST FIX during implementation. Add to task-5 acceptance criteria: 'warn counters are only incremented when the push succeeds (all validation layers pass)'.

risks.title: Mixed-outcome push: some files warned, some files blocked
risks.description: A single push can contain files A (first violation, would warn) and B (second violation, would block). The current design blocks the entire push if ANY file exceeds the threshold. This means file A never gets pushed even though it was only at the warning stage. The agent may be confused about which file caused the block.
risks.mitigation: The error message should clearly list which files are at the 'warn' stage and which are at the 'block' stage. The current architect design (DD-8) includes blocked files and allowed patterns in the error, which is sufficient. The agent can self-correct by removing file B from the push.

risks.title: Planner produces too-narrow file lists, causing agents to spin on restrictions
risks.description: Planners (LLM agents) may not anticipate all files an implementation task needs. Common misses: config files (pyproject.toml, package.json, Makefile), __init__.py files in new packages, migration files, generated files (lock files), and helper modules that need modification. With recursive directory expansion, the risk is partially mitigated for files in already-listed directories. But files in completely unlisted directories will trigger warn-then-block.
risks.mitigation: Three-layer defense: (1) directory expansion grants recursive subtree access for listed files' directories, (2) warn-then-block gives agents one free pass per file, (3) plan template guidance (task-7) instructs planners to list generously. If still problematic post-launch, add an implicit root-config allowlist as a non-breaking follow-up. The deferred escape hatch (DD-4) is the ultimate safety valve.
risks.recommendation: Monitor violation logs post-launch. Track ratio of warned vs blocked pushes. If >20% of implement pushes trigger warnings, the feature is too restrictive and needs adjustment.

risks.title: Path traversal via malicious allowed_files entries
risks.description: If the orchestrator passes attacker-controlled paths in allowed_files (e.g., `../../../etc/passwd` or `/etc/shadow`), the PhaseFileRestriction matcher might match unexpected paths. The orchestrator computes allowed_files from the contract's files_affected field, which is populated from plan YAML parsed by the planner agent.
risks.mitigation: PhaseFileRestriction._normalize_path() (phase_filter.py:216-228) blocks paths starting with `../` or `/`. The normalization runs on the FILE being pushed, not on the pattern. However, the pattern itself (`allowed_files` entries) is not normalized. A pattern like `../etc/*` would be passed to fnmatch but would never match a normalized file path (since normalized paths can't start with `../`). Additional defense: task-2 acceptance criteria require validation of allowed_files entries at session creation (reject empty strings, non-strings). Recommend also rejecting patterns containing `../` or starting with `/` at the session creation endpoint.
risks.recommendation: Add input validation for allowed_files patterns in the /sessions/create handler: reject entries containing `..` or starting with `/`. This is a ~3 line addition to task-2.

risks.title: Session.allowed_files becomes stale if plan is amended after container spawn
risks.description: allowed_files is computed once at container spawn time and persisted on the session. If the plan is amended during implementation (e.g., via HITL decision), the session's allowed_files is not updated. The agent operates under stale restrictions.
risks.mitigation: Plan amendments during implementation are rare — plans are finalized before the implement phase begins. The architect correctly identifies this as a known limitation (edge case 'Session allowed_files becomes stale'). A session update endpoint is deferred to follow-up. Gateway restart does NOT help because allowed_files is persisted.

risks.title: Gateway restart resets _warned_files (transient counters)
risks.description: The _warned_files dict is transient and not persisted. Gateway restarts reset all counters, giving agents fresh warning allowances. An agent that was at the block threshold before restart gets another free pass.
risks.mitigation: Fail-open on restart is acceptable per the 'guide, don't cage' philosophy (DD-5). Gateway restarts during agent sessions are rare. The worst case is an extra free pass, which is consistent with the gradual enforcement philosophy.

risks.title: Breaking existing Session tests due to new fields
risks.description: Adding `allowed_files: list[str] | None = None` and `_warned_files: dict[str, int]` to the Session dataclass could break tests that construct Sessions without these fields or that assert on to_dict_for_persistence() output.
risks.mitigation: Both fields have defaults (None and {} respectively), so existing Session constructors are backward compatible. to_dict_for_persistence() uses conditional inclusion (`if X is not None`), so existing test assertions on the output won't see unexpected keys when allowed_files is None. _warned_files is not persisted at all. Task-8 explicitly tests backward compatibility. Risk is minimal.

risks.title: Warned push succeeds — out-of-scope file is permanently in git history
risks.description: When the per-task layer warns on the first violation, the push succeeds and the out-of-scope file is committed to the branch. This file is now in git history. Even if the agent self-corrects on subsequent pushes, the file from the warned push remains. The integrator or reviewer would need to clean it up.
risks.mitigation: This is intentional per the 'guide, don't cage' philosophy. The post-agent auto-commit (task-6) provides a safety net for uncommitted out-of-scope files. For committed files, the integrator agent in the Tier 3 cycle already reviews cross-contamination. The alternative (blocking on first attempt) would frequently block agents on planner oversights.

risks.title: Directory expansion scope explosion for shallow directory files
risks.description: Directory expansion converts each explicit file path `dir/file.py` to the pattern `dir/*`. Because fnmatch is recursive, this grants access to the ENTIRE `dir/` subtree. For files in shallow directories, this creates disproportionately broad access. Example: if a task lists `src/constants.py`, expansion adds `src/*` which matches `src/auth/login.py`, `src/payments/checkout.py`, and every other file under `src/`. A single root-level file in a common directory effectively neutralizes per-task restrictions for that entire subtree. Independently verified: fnmatch.fnmatch('src/payments/checkout.py', 'src/*') returns True.
risks.mitigation: The architect acknowledges recursive matching but does not call out this specific 'scope explosion' scenario. The practical impact depends on project layout: monorepos with deep directory structures (src/auth/, src/payments/) get useful containment even with recursive matching, because the expansion is at the leaf directory level. Projects with files directly under src/ get weaker containment. Two possible implementation-time mitigations: (1) Only expand to `dir/*` for the IMMEDIATE parent directory of each listed file (already the plan), which naturally scopes to leaf directories for deep paths. (2) Consider adding only the explicit file paths WITHOUT directory expansion when the parent is a top-level source directory (e.g., `src/`). Option (2) is more complex and may not be worth it for v1.
risks.recommendation: Add a test case in task-9 that explicitly demonstrates this scope explosion scenario (file at `src/constants.py` granting access to `src/deep/nested/thing.py`). This ensures the behavior is documented and consciously accepted, not accidentally overlooked. Consider logging a structured warning when directory expansion produces a pattern with fewer than 2 path segments (e.g., `src/*`) since these are disproportionately broad.

risks.title: Concurrent push handling and _warned_files thread safety
risks.description: The _warned_files dict on the Session object is modified during push handling. If the gateway runs with multiple threads (e.g., Flask with threaded=True), concurrent pushes from the same session could race on dict read/modify/write. However, concurrent pushes from a single agent session are extremely rare — Claude Code makes sequential git pushes.
risks.mitigation: Flask's default development server is single-threaded. The production gateway likely uses a WSGI server that may be multi-threaded, but concurrent pushes from the same session are improbable (agents push sequentially). If this becomes a concern, a threading.Lock per session or using collections.Counter (atomic increment) would resolve it. Not worth adding complexity for v1.

risks.title: Error message confusion between validation layers
risks.description: With 4 validation layers (role-based, agent-role, per-task, phase), agents may receive errors from different layers on successive pushes, making it hard to understand which restriction to address. For example, fixing a per-task violation might expose an underlying phase restriction that was masked.
risks.mitigation: DD-10 orders layers from most-specific to least-specific, and each layer has distinct error messages. The per-task error specifically mentions 'per-task file restriction' and includes allowed_files patterns. Phase errors mention the phase name. Agent-role errors mention the role. The agent should be able to distinguish them.

risks.title: Large allowed_files lists from complex plans
risks.description: Plans with many tasks and many files per task could produce large allowed_files lists (100+ entries). Each push validation iterates all patterns for each changed file.
risks.mitigation: Architect correctly estimates 100 patterns x 50 files = 5000 comparisons as negligible (<10ms). Session persistence adds a small JSON field. No optimization needed.

disagreements_with_architect.architect_position: DD-1 specifies warn on first push, block on second. No mention of interaction with subsequent validation layers.
disagreements_with_architect.risk_analyst_position: The implementation MUST ensure warn counters are only incremented when the overall push succeeds. Otherwise, pushes that fail at later layers (phase restrictions) consume the agent's warning allowance without providing any benefit. This is a correctness issue that should be added to task-5 acceptance criteria.
disagreements_with_architect.recommendation: Add to task-5 acceptance: 'Warn counters (_warned_files) are only incremented after all validation layers pass. The per-task layer returns pending warnings that are committed by the push handler on overall success.'

disagreements_with_architect.architect_position: Planner responsibility with documentation guidance. No implicit allowlist.
disagreements_with_architect.risk_analyst_position: Acceptable for v1 given the warn-then-block safety net, but this will likely need revisiting. Root-level config files (pyproject.toml, package.json, Makefile, tsconfig.json) are modified by many tasks but rarely listed in files_affected because they're 'infrastructure' rather than 'feature' files. The first few production pipeline runs will likely show high warning rates on config files. Recommend tracking this metric.
disagreements_with_architect.recommendation: If >30% of per-task warnings are for root-level config files in the first 2 weeks, create a follow-up issue for an implicit config allowlist.

disagreements_with_architect.architect_position: Per-task checks run after agent-role (Layer 2) and before phase (Layer 3).
disagreements_with_architect.risk_analyst_position: Running per-task checks BEFORE phase checks means per-task warnings fire even for files that would be blocked by phase restrictions anyway. While the counter-increment fix (D-1) prevents the worst outcome, agents would still see confusing per-task warning messages for files that are fundamentally blocked by phase. Running per-task AFTER phase would avoid this: phase blocks first, then per-task only checks files that passed phase. However, the architect's ordering has the advantage of showing per-task violations early, which helps agents learn their scope. Acceptable either way.
disagreements_with_architect.recommendation: The ordering is acceptable if R-2 (counter increment timing) is fixed. If not fixed, this becomes a blocking issue.

path_traversal.details: PhaseFileRestriction._normalize_path() (phase_filter.py:216-228) blocks paths with `../` or leading `/`. This runs on pushed files. Recommend also validating allowed_files patterns at session creation (task-2) to reject patterns containing `..` as defense-in-depth.

privilege_escalation.details: Per-task restrictions only NARROW access (additive to phase restrictions per DD-6). They cannot grant access beyond what phase restrictions allow. A file must pass ALL layers.

injection_via_allowed_files.details: allowed_files entries are used as fnmatch patterns. Fnmatch patterns do not support regex or shell injection. Malformed patterns (e.g., `[`, `]`) would cause fnmatch to fail to match, resulting in a more restrictive (not less restrictive) behavior. The worst case is a pattern that matches nothing, which blocks all files — fail-closed.

bypass_via_gateway_restart.details: Gateway restart resets _warned_files counters (DD-5). Fail-open by design. An attacker with gateway restart access has broader control anyway.

backward_compatibility.details: All new fields have defaults (allowed_files=None, _warned_files={}). Session.from_persistence() uses .get() for optional fields. Existing sessions load correctly. to_dict_for_persistence() conditionally includes allowed_files only when non-None. No API contract changes for existing callers.

forward_compatibility.details: The design supports future extensions: (1) escape hatch via session update endpoint (DD-4), (2) implicit config allowlist (DD-3 follow-up), (3) segment-aware matching behind feature flag (DD-2 follow-up), (4) per-task restrictions for other agent roles. None of these require breaking changes.

existing_test_impact.details: Existing tests construct Sessions without allowed_files — backward compatible due to None default. Existing phase restriction tests in test_phase_filter_restrictions.py are unaffected (different code path). Post-agent commit tests may need minor updates if the function signature changes (new allowed_files parameter).

rollback_plan.immediate_disable: Set EGG_TASK_FILE_WARN_THRESHOLD=999 to effectively disable blocking (warn threshold never reached). This preserves logging for monitoring.
rollback_plan.full_disable: Stop passing allowed_files from the spawner (_compute_allowed_files returns None). No code revert needed — the enforcement layers gracefully handle None.
rollback_plan.strict_mode_revert: Set EGG_TASK_FILE_RESTRICTIONS_ENFORCE=false (the default) to return to warn-then-block from strict mode.
phased_rollout_recommendation: Week 1: Deploy with warn-only (default config). Monitor violation logs. Measure warning rates per pipeline.
Week 2: If warning rates are acceptable (<20% of pushes), keep default threshold=1. If high, investigate planner guidance or add config allowlist.
Week 3+: Consider enabling strict mode (ENFORCE=true) for mature planners that consistently produce complete file lists.

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: The automatic directory expansion (`dir/*`) from explicit file paths can create disproportionately broad access for files in shallow directories. Human should decide if this tradeoff is acceptable or if expansion should be depth-limited.
areas_requiring_human_review.decision_needed: Accept recursive expansion for all directory depths, or add special handling for shallow directories (e.g., skip expansion when parent has fewer than 2 path segments)?

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: The architect's design doesn't specify when counters increment relative to other validation layers. Implementation must handle this correctly or agents lose warning allowances on failed pushes.
areas_requiring_human_review.decision_needed: Confirm that task-5 implementation should only increment counters after all layers pass.

areas_requiring_human_review.reason: The 'planner responsibility' decision may cause friction in practice. Root-level config files are commonly modified but rarely listed explicitly.
areas_requiring_human_review.decision_needed: Accept planner-only approach for v1, or add a small implicit allowlist of common root config files?

test_coverage_assessment.assessment: The architect's revision 2 addresses both blocking test gaps from the reviewer. The test plan is comprehensive: Session persistence round-trip (task-8), push validation with explicit recursive matching verification (task-9), post-agent commit filtering (task-10), orchestrator compute_allowed_files (task-11), and integration tier-3 dispatch (test plan entry). Recommend adding two additional test cases.

additional_test_recommendations.test: Scope explosion: file at src/constants.py expands to src/* which matches src/deep/nested/thing.py
additional_test_recommendations.reason: Documents and verifies the R-10 risk explicitly, ensuring the behavior is conscious and not accidental

additional_test_recommendations.test: Warn counter not incremented when push fails at phase restriction layer
additional_test_recommendations.reason: Verifies R-2 fix: counters should only increment on overall push success

highest_risk_tasks.reason: Core enforcement logic with multiple interaction points: counter management, deferred counter commits (R-2 fix), strict mode toggle, checkpoint bypass, error message formatting. Most complex single task.

Requires loading contract, filtering tasks by plan_phase_id, computing union, applying directory expansion. The plan_phase_id plumbing through _spawn_and_wait to spawn_agent_container adds cross-file coordination.

conditions: R-2 (warn counter timing) must be fixed at implementation time — add to task-5 acceptance criteria
R-5 (path traversal in patterns) — add pattern validation to task-2 (reject entries with `..`)
R-10 (scope explosion) — add explicit test case documenting the behavior

Track per-task block rate (blocked pushes / total pushes per pipeline)
Log which files trigger warnings most frequently (identify planner training gaps)
